exposure: Anaesthetic service provider type (specialist vs. non-specialist)
Method of testing level of block
Management strategy for failed spinal anaesthesia (e.g., convert to GA, repeat spinal, administer IV drugs)
outcome: Standardised approach to testing level of block
Standardised approach to management of failed spinal anaesthesia
Likelihood of converting to general anaesthetic (GA)
Likelihood of repeating spinal anaesthesia or administering intravenous ketamine, midazolam and opioids
Method of assessment of block height
Self-reported competence to perform a GA
Agreement on usefulness of a 'failed' spinal algorithm
cohort: Obstetric anaesthetic service providers, including interns to specialist anaesthetists, from 51 government hospitals in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.
finding: There is no standardized approach to testing the level of block or managing failed spinal anaesthesia for CS in South Africa, with significant differences observed between specialist and non-specialist anaesthetists.
mod_finding: The study reveals a lack of standardization and differing management strategies among anaesthetic providers for failed spinal anaesthesia during caesarean sections.
